subject: Physical jurisdiction and tenant wipe verification protocol
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@medicore.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tenant deletion evidence and jurisdictional custody question

Vivek —

Thanks for taking this. We are preparing for a regulatory audit and need to confirm how Redwood handles customer-controlled storage in Private/VPC deployments for data residency and deletion. Specifically: 

- When a tenant asks for a full wipe, what artefacts do you provide as proof of deletion? (snapshots removed, object-store tombstone logs, snapshot hashes, runbook execution logs, notary statements, etc.)
- How do you demonstrate physical jurisdiction of data at rest (e.g., region-bound storage, non-replication outside declared region)?
- What is the key custody model at deletion time — can customers hold the KMS keys or require key-handback + crypto-sanitize?

We need a short list of acceptable evidence types (for our auditors) and expected timelines for an expedited erase (48–72 hours vs standard 7–14 days). Please CC anyone on your side who owns the ops/runbook.

Appreciate a clear, bulleted response we can include in our audit pack.

—Daniel Park
Director, Security & Compliance
MedicoRe

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Tenant deletion evidence and jurisdictional custody question

Thanks Daniel — jumping in with a concise answer and the runbook stub attached. I own the product/ps escalation for Private deployments — Marissa (CS) and Karthik (Solutions) are looped for scheduling and contract specifics.

High-level: we support customer-controlled storage in Private/VPC deployments with a few supported evidence types and tooling paths. Short bullets below, followed by next steps.

Evidence types we can provide (we typically deliver 2–3 of these, depending on customer preference):
- Object-store tombstone logs (immutable audit view) — includes object IDs, delete events, and timestamps.
- Snapshot deletion manifest + proof-of-nonreplication (snapshot hashes, manifest signed by the Redwood control plane).
- Execution logs from the wipe-runbook (operator id, runbook steps, duration, return codes).
- KMS key rotation / destruction statement (if customer allows Redwood to manage rekeying/rotation prior to wipe).
- Optional: notarized deletion certificate / witnessed delete (we coordinate on-site or third-party notarization if required).

Jurisdiction / geofencing: Private deployments run in customer-controlled VPCs or customer VPCs in a selected region. We enforce placement by default and do not replicate tenant data outside the configured region. For extra assurance we can provide:
- Region-bound placement report (which AZs/regions host tenant volumes)
- Snapshot location manifest with region tags

Key custody: two supported models:
1) Customer-managed keys (recommended for the highest guarantee): customer holds the KMS/HSM keys. Redwood cannot decrypt or rehydrate data without key access. On deletion, customer rotates/zeroes keys and provides proof of key change.
2) Redwood-managed keys with audited rotation: Redwood performs key rotation/crypto-sanitize and provides a signed rotation/destruction statement.

Timelines:
- Expedited erase path (customer agrees to a pre-defined canary runbook + Redwood ops window): 48–72 hours to provide deletion artefacts (subject to scope and size).
- Standard tenant-sunset process: 7–14 days (includes backup retention window and ticketed verification).

Attachments: vpc-data-handshake.pdf (runbook summary), wipe-runbook-ops.txt (ops log format).

Next steps: please confirm which evidence types your auditors will accept and whether you prefer customer-managed keys. If you want notarized deletion, Marissa will propose options and rough costs.

—Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: vpc-data-handshake.pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-06-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant deletion evidence and jurisdictional custody question

Daniel — adding operational detail and options for the audit pack.

Operational options we can offer:
1) Remote evidence bundle (no onsite): includes tombstone logs, snapshot manifest + hashes, runbook execution logs, and signed KMS rotation statement (if Redwood-managed). Delivery SLA: 48–72 hours for standard-size tenants (<5TB); larger tenants will be scoped.
2) Witnessed deletion (on-site or video witness): our ops lead executes the runbook with a MedicoRe witness. We capture a live screen recording, a signed deletion certificate, and a timestamped witness attestation. SLA: typically scheduling + execution within 5 business days.
3) Notarized third-party attestation: we coordinate with your legal team to generate a deletion certificate that your notary can sign; take ~7–10 business days including sign-off.

Evidence format details (for auditors):
- Tombstone logs: CSV export with object_id, delete_timestamp (UTC), operator_id, and hash.
- Snapshot manifest: JSON list with snapshot_id, region, object_hashes, signed_by (control-plane-sig).
- Runbook: text file with step-by-step commands, start/stop timestamps, and exit codes.

Legal/contract items: if you require retention windows shorter than our standard backups, we need a signed amendment to override default backup policies. Karthik, can you follow up on amendment language / pricing?

Happy to jump on a quick 30m call to align auditors and pick the preferred evidence package.

—Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: wipe-runbook-ops.txt)

Thanks Vivek / Marissa — that is helpful. A few clarifications from our auditors and legal: 

- MedicoRe prefers customer-managed keys where possible. Can you confirm the exact steps we should take to rotate/retire keys such that Redwood’s control plane cannot rehydrate snapshots? Do you have a short checklist we can run?
- For the tombstone logs: do they include object checksums (we need to match against our exported object list)?
- For snapshot manifests: can the signed manifest be sha256-signed and timestamped with an RFC3161 timestamp (or equivalent)?

Also, legal asks for a sample attestation template we can sign off on. If you can send a templated document we’ll review and return with redlines.

—Daniel

Subject: Re: Tenant deletion evidence and jurisdictional custody question

Daniel — thanks, quick answers and commitments from the solutions side.

Checklist for customer-managed keys (short):
1) Generate new key version (or import into your KMS) and rotate application keys so Redwood cannot access old ciphertext.
2) Trigger a key-disable or schedule key-destruction per your KMS provider. Provide Redwood with the key rotation transaction id for our audit log.
3) Initiate the wipe-runbook (we will accept the rotation id as proof of crypto-sanitize if keys are customer-controlled).

Tombstone logs: yes — CSV includes object_id, sha256_checksum, size_bytes, delete_timestamp_utc, operator_id.

Signed manifests: we can produce an RFC3161-compatible timestamp and sign the manifest with our control-plane signing key; we will provide both the signed manifest and the timestamp token.

Attestation template: attached (attestation-template.docx). We can accept your redlines.

Commitment: if MedicoRe confirms customer-managed-keys + expedited evidence bundle, Redwood will provision the evidence package (tombstone CSV + signed snapshot manifest + runbook logs) within 72 hours of runbook execution. If you want a witness/notary, we will coordinate dates and provide pricing.

Please confirm which path you want to take and the desired SLAs. We will open a support ticket (SUP-56421) and include the deliverables checklist.

—Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: attestation-template.docx)
